rootCause: Synchronous snapshots ignored expiration. Local writes updated only the writer cache. API-only startup returned before settings warmup. Maintenance errors fell through to normal handling.
beforeFlow: MongoDB -> process-local cache -> synchronous policy consumers, with no cross-worker invalidation and no expiration check on synchronous reads.
afterFlow: MongoDB compare-and-swap write -> writer cache and opaque Redis revision token -> jittered worker revision checks -> fresh MongoDB read -> local policy snapshot. API readiness awaits Mongo warmup. Request middleware revalidates before security gates.

consistency.redisContents: Opaque invalidation token only, scoped by database name
consistency.writes: Fresh authoritative read, monotonic updatedAt compare-and-swap and up to four conflict retries. Local generation prevents overlapping reads from replacing a completed write. A timestamp guard prevents out-of-order write responses from replacing newer local snapshots.
consistency.staleEvents: Tokens carry no settings payload. Every token change re-reads MongoDB. Older tokens cannot install older settings.
consistency.outage: Periodic MongoDB revalidation continues independently of Redis. Failed revalidation cannot extend snapshot expiry. Expired synchronous reads throw and API requests return 503 if fresh settings cannot be loaded.
consistency.coldStart: Pre-start configuration consumers retain defaults. Both API startup modes await authoritative warmup before listening.
consistency.shutdown: Settings timer is cleared and no new settings tick is scheduled after stop. Existing Redis lifecycle remains responsible for its shared client.
consistency.implementationChoice: Revision polling uses the existing bounded Redis command client, avoiding an additional subscription connection. No new dependency or schema field.

multiWorkerEvidence.infrastructure: Independent forked Node.js processes, disposable MongoDB replica set and actual Redis 7.0.15 in WSL on loopback port 27391

Maintenance exemptions retain their existing path contracts when settings are available.

limitations: Pre-start configuration defaults remain available to direct service consumers. New API entry points must await settings initialization and revalidate before policy-dependent handling.
